## Scope and evidence

Live SELECT-only inspection of observe_main on observe.ultreia.io, performed on 12 November 2026.

Server application: 10.0.8; persistence model: 10.0; PostgreSQL: 18.6.

The prepared queries read actual observation rows, not just table definitions or reference catalogues.

Queries used separate statement snapshots. No database records were changed and every API session was closed.

The saved aggregate results and SQL provide the evidence; no passwords, tokens or security files are included.

```text
/home/tchemit/.cache/ros.form.observe/ird/analyses/20261112T211733Z
```

Use the [sheet reviews](ll-sheet-reviews.html) for field-level reasoning and the remaining reporting decisions.

## Selection reproduced

Philippe's trip query names five programmes. Most detail queries name only IRD, CAPRUN and TAAF.

The analysis profiles all five explicit trip-query IDs; it does not execute the legacy export queries.

Its R parameters select FRA vessels, the Indian Ocean, and trips starting or ending in 2025.

All 67 matching trips also survive the trip query's required reference joins.

All operations of those trips are retained; this is a source-coverage assessment, not a reproduced Excel export.

| Programme                          | All matching trips | 2025 FRA / Indian trips |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------- |
| DCF Longline (IRD)                 | 1,006              | 67                      |
| CAPPER                             | 11                 | 0                       |
| DCF Longline (CAPRUN)              | 0                  | 0                       |
| DCF Longline (TAAF)                | 2                  | 0                       |
| DCF Longline (Mayotte marine park) | 22                 | 0                       |
| Total                              | 1,041              | 67                      |

The full five-programme scope contains 6,501 sets and 117,680 catch rows, including years outside 2025.

The detailed findings below apply to the 67-trip 2025 selection unless explicitly stated otherwise.

### Observation method matters

| Recorded method        | Trips | Sets | Catch rows | Grouped weights | Length measurements |
| ---------------------- | ----- | ---- | ---------- | --------------- | ------------------- |
| OB: observer-monitored | 17    | 147  | 5,231      | 0               | 4,023               |
| SR: self-reporting     | 50    | 314  | 3,472      | 1,350           | 0                   |
| Total                  | 67    | 461  | 8,703      | 1,350           | 4,023               |

All length measurements belong to observer-monitored trips. All grouped weights belong to self-reporting trips.

The SR group includes 12 individual catch entries and 3,460 grouped entries; OB has only individual entries.

Programme membership alone therefore does not establish the collection method or the ROS sampling protocol.

Whether SR trips belong in this export is a selection/reporting decision; neither group was silently excluded.

## Reusable information and limits

| Source fact            | 2025 selection                    | Use or remaining condition                                    |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Trip methods           | 17 OB; 50 SR                      | Decide inclusion separately from programme selection.         |
| Grouped catch weights  | 1,350 records; 49 trips           | 1,123 have specified processing and method; all are SR.       |
| Additional lengths     | 10 individuals; 7 trips           | SCL and SCW for the same turtle, not separate specimens.      |
| Length tools           | 2,883 known; 1,140 unknown        | Use the recorded tool; do not force calliper.                 |
| Tags                   | 1 individual                      | Identifier candidate; deployment/recovery still unknown.      |
| Photo references       | 1,267 catches                     | References exist; file existence and format unchecked.        |
| Hook sizes             | 293 known; 530 unknown; 2 missing | Actual known sizes are usable mapping inputs.                 |
| Floatline lengths      | 1,992 rows; all 461 sets          | 333 sets exceed three distinct lengths; 18 contain zero.      |
| Branchline composition | 1 row per set; 100% MON leader    | Global composition exists; section interpretation is open.    |
| Individual weights     | 0 records                         | No individual-weight export for this selection.               |
| Mitigation selections  | 0 records                         | No evidence from this association; absence of use not proved. |
| Maturity               | 0 populated values                | No maturity export demonstrated for this selection.           |

A populated source value is a mapping input. It is not, by itself, an approved ROS value or complete target row.

### Weights

The 1,350 positive grouped weights span 49 trips and 311 sets, with values from 2 to 2,724 kg.

There are 1,347 records with both type and method references; 224 of those use Unknown processing.

This leaves 1,123 records with a specified processing type and method, and three with a missing method.

Recorded methods are visual assessment for 1,268 rows and scales for 79; the other three have no method.

Preserve estimated versus weighed status and processing. Do not report these totals as individual fish weights.

The wider five-programme scope has 741 individual weight measurements outside this 2025 selection.

### Specimens and tags

The 4,023 lengths belong to 4,013 individuals. All sizes are positive, from 29 to 325 cm, with no fractions here.

Ten turtles have two distinct measures, SCL and SCW: six TTL and four TUG records, across seven trips.

Those pairs can inform the two length fields while preserving one specimen identity; code mapping remains necessary.

Tools are calliper for 2,876 measures, ruler for four, tape for two and visual assessment for one.

Another 1,140 measures explicitly record Unknown; a constant calliper would misstate those observations.

One measured ALB individual has a five-character, identifier-like tag value. Tag-event semantics remain unverified.

Photo references exist on 1,267 catches, and sample references on 72. These are not verified files or sample metadata.

### Gear

All 295 hook-composition records on OB trips have a known size except two missing sizes.

All 530 SR hook-composition records explicitly reference Unknown size; non-null counts would conceal this gap.

At set level, 145 sets have all sizes known, two have partial size coverage and 314 have no known size.

The 461 global branchline compositions each cover 100%, with MON leader material and lengths from 1.5 to 17.1 m.

Leader length is populated in 147 compositions. Individual branchline dimensions and material are empty.

The 1,992 floatline records cover every set, with two to eight records per set and proportions summing to 100%.

There are 333 sets with more than three distinct lengths. The form's three length slots need a representation rule.

Eighteen sets contain a zero length; its meaning needs review rather than conversion into a fabricated length.

Shooter use is true on 21 sets. Twenty have speeds, all on SR trips; the one OB case lacks its speed.

Clip-on timing has 122 populated values. Snap and swivel weights have 264 and 70 populated values respectively.

Those component weights do not establish average sinker weight, weighted percentages or hook-to-sinker distances.

The mitigation association has no rows throughout the five-programme scope, not just within the 2025 selection.

The 209,430 individual branchline records in 2025 have no positive cut-off or hook-loss flags.

Their false defaults do not establish observed zero bite-offs or complete observer coverage.

### Trip references and operational fields

All 67 trips have linked observers, captains, departure and landing ports, with port LOCODEs and coordinates.

Vessel IOTC IDs are populated for 66 trips; crew count for 17. ROS registry matching remains separate.

All 461 sets have setting and hauling endpoint times and positions within valid coordinate ranges.

No reversed start/end timestamps were found. This does not establish their time zone or verify geographic accuracy.

Catch counts are positive; individual-mode catches all have count one. Sampling protocol still needs evidence.

## What this changes

Several optional values omitted by Philippe are populated and can become export inputs after verified correspondence.

The strongest candidates are grouped weights, paired lengths, recorded tools, photo references and the tag identifier.

The two collection methods explain major coverage differences and should remain explicit in the next review.

Individual weights, mitigation membership and maturity cannot be recovered from these sources for the 2025 selection.

Unknown hook sizes, bait preparation, excess floatline lengths and missing observation context still need decisions.

The review does not approve mappings, infer missing observations, implement an exporter or claim a valid full workbook.

## Reproduction

The evidence directory contains SQL, aggregate JSON results, provenance and SHA-256 checksums.

The saved selection IDs and denominators allow the same checks to be repeated without running Philippe's exporter.

Source units are confirmed by ObServe's observation UI labels: sizes in cm and weights in kg.

CatchAcquisitionMode defines individual as ordinal 0 and grouped as ordinal 1.

See source label keys for Catch.totalWeight, SizeMeasure.size and WeightMeasure.weight in services_en_GB.properties.
